solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Love given to cleaner reforming strict policy

indicators.note: something being reformed is remade in a new shape, so the word before it is rearranged

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis scoring
taken as written
the seven letters of this word, rearranged

explanation.surface: A sweetheart hands a cleaner a new, stricter set of house rules.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis, love means a score of nothing; 'given' merely joins it to the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Zero tolerance is a policy of punishing every infringement, however minor, without exception.

clue.text: Believer in Arizona sort that needs conversion

indicators.note: converting something turns it into a different form, so the letters before must be re-formed

blocks.note: all eleven letters of these two words

explanation.surface: An Arizona type who needs to be converted to some faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conversion' fits the religious surface neatly, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A Zoroastrian follows the ancient Persian religion founded by the prophet Zoroaster, so is a religious adherent.

clue.text: Fleet applying pressure in attack

indicators.note: the pressure sits inside the attack, so one goes within the other

blocks.note: P is the symbol for pressure in physics
a raid is a sudden attack

explanation.surface: A navy applies pressure during an assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleet' looks like a navy, but here it is the adjective meaning swift.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleet as an adjective means swift or nimble on foot, so it matches very quick movement.

clue.text: Australian bird‘s hangover symptom?

blocks.note: first meaning: a songbird of Australasia, also called a whistler
second meaning: the muzzy, heavy feeling after too much drink

explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'; the question mark flags the jokey idea of a bird with a hangover. THICKHEAD is both a bird name and a sore, foggy head.
explanation.definitionFit: The thickhead is a genuine Australian bird family, and a thick head is the dull ache felt the morning after drinking.

clue.text: Unimaginative drunk left after considerable time

indicators.note: this word places the letter for left behind the period of time

blocks.note: lit is slang for intoxicated
an era is a long period
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone dull who got drunk and left after a long time at the party.
explanation.definitionFit: A literal mind takes words at face value, lacking imagination or any figurative flair.

clue.text: Painter Foster’s spilled a thinner on the ground

indicators.note: what is spilled is lost from the container, so the letter named next is dropped

blocks.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword painter
to foster a child is to rear it
the letter that is lost

explanation.surface: An artist called Foster spilled some paint thinner on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: Read Foster's as 'Foster has': the verb has spilled its letter A. Foster's is also an Australian lager, a likely red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Something thinner on the ground is scarcer, less commonly met with, which is what rarer means.

clue.text: Speed up Bletchley Park genius, providing support

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the word from bottom to top

blocks.note: to run is to speed along
Alan Turing broke codes at Bletchley Park, the British wartime codebreaking centre

explanation.surface: Hurry up the brilliant codebreaker, who will then help.
explanation.definitionFit: Nurturing is caring for and encouraging growth, which amounts to giving support to someone.

clue.text: Cold-blooded creature clever duke abandoned

indicators.note: the duke is abandoned, so his letter is left out

blocks.note: deft means skilful
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A heartless schemer whom a smart duke has deserted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold-blooded' sounds like a ruthless person, but it describes an amphibian.
explanation.definitionFit: An eft is a young newt, an amphibian whose body temperature follows its surroundings.

clue.text: Stole hit repeatedly broadcast

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard over the air, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: to rap is to knock again and again

explanation.surface: A thief keeps striking, and it is all over the news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stole' looks like the past tense of steal; it is the noun, a shawl.
explanation.definitionFit: A stole is a long scarf worn over the shoulders, a garment also called a wrap.

clue.text: Paraphrases vignette — proper text is regularly ignored

indicators.note: dropping every other letter in a steady pattern leaves only the alternate ones

blocks.note: keep the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on

explanation.surface: A short sketch rewords things, so the correct text gets overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts with the I of vignette and takes in the final word is.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpret a passage is to render its meaning in other words, as a paraphrase does.

clue.text: Cook entertains news boss and European publisher

indicators.note: a host who entertains has guests inside the home, so the cook holds the rest

blocks.note: a baker is a cook of bread
ED is short for editor
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A chef hosts a newspaper editor and a European book publisher.
explanation.walkthrough: Karl Baedeker was a German publisher famous for travel guidebooks.
explanation.definitionFit: Baedeker was the nineteenth-century German firm and founder whose travel guides became a byword for them.

clue.text: OS showing circuitous routes?

blocks.note: first meaning: read as O's, circles or round shapes
second meaning: the regular circuits of a postman or doctor

explanation.walkthrough: OS looks like Ordnance Survey, Britain's map-maker, which suits routes; it is the plural of the letter O, each a round.
explanation.definitionFit: An O is a circle and so a round, while rounds are also the circular routes made on regular visits.

clue.text: Unable to catch fast doe running without delay inside

indicators.note: a running animal is in motion, so its letters move about
the phrase meaning promptly sits within the jumbled letters

blocks.note: the seven letters to be jumbled
ASAP stands for as soon as possible

explanation.surface: A deer running off too quickly to be caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unable to catch' suggests a hunter, but it means unable to hear.
explanation.definitionFit: Deaf as a post is an idiom for completely deaf, so such a person cannot catch what is said.

clue.text: Approve recording 50 in random sporting format

indicators.note: the earlier pieces are placed within the word for random

blocks.note: a stray bullet is a random one
to OK something is to approve it
an EP is an extended-play record
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Signing off a recording of fifty songs in a haphazard sports competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recording' tempts as a full record, but the short extended-play format is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Stroke play is the golf format where total shots over the round decide the winner, as opposed to match play.

clue.text: Everyone in Rome crowds quartet there: men who’d take it all in?

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for 'those who would take everything in'

indicators.note: to crowd something is to hem it in all round, so the Latin word surrounds the rest

blocks.note: omnes is Latin for all people
four as a Roman numeral, there meaning in Rome
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A Roman crowd surrounding a quartet of men who will swallow anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There' refers back to Rome, so the quartet is written in Roman numerals; men are other ranks, the army's ordinary soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Omnivores eat both plants and animals, taking in all kinds of food rather than specialising.

clue.text: Long drink in beer garden?

definitions.note: read whimsically as a yard belonging to ale

blocks.note: first meaning: a tall glass holding about three pints, downed as a challenge
second meaning: a yard, or garden, of beer, taken literally

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical reading of a garden as a yard and beer as ale.
explanation.definitionFit: A yard of ale is a yard-long glass and the beer in it, here also read as a patch of ground for beer.

clue.text: Academician getting measure of wit around Asian land

indicators.note: the measure goes all round the academician, enclosing him

blocks.note: IQ is the intelligence quotient
RA is a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A scholar gets his cleverness assessed somewhere in Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Iraq is a country in western Asia, in the Middle East between Iran and Syria.

clue.text: Jack at hostelry serves spirits

blocks.note: J is the jack in a pack of cards
an inn is a hostelry

explanation.surface: A man called Jack working at a pub pours out the spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirits' suggests drink at the bar, but they are supernatural beings.
explanation.definitionFit: Jinn are the supernatural beings of Arabian and Islamic lore, a plural word for genies.

clue.text: Branching chart complete: right to divide dog and sheep

indicators.note: to divide the dog the pieces must split it apart, so they go in the middle

blocks.note: taken as written
to complete is to end
R is the abbreviation for right
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A tree diagram of sheepdog bloodlines, finished off with a dividing line.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'complete' and 'right' do the dividing, entering the dog after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A dendrogram is a tree-shaped diagram showing how items cluster or are related, so a chart that branches.

clue.text: Horse adopted by Pathan represented fiery mixture

indicators.note: something adopted is taken into a family, so it goes inside the other letters
to be represented is to be shown in another form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: horse is slang for heroin, whose abbreviation is H
the six letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A Pathan tribesman takes on a horse with a fiery temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: A Pathan is a Pashtun of Afghanistan or Pakistan.
explanation.definitionFit: Naphtha is a flammable blend of liquid hydrocarbons, used in incendiaries, so a mixture that burns.

clue.text: The wine in Provence is sent back? Complain tearfully

indicators.note: a bottle sent back returns the way it came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: le vin is French for the wine
is shortened to 's

explanation.surface: A diner in France whines and weeps after sending back the wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Provence is a region of France, so its language supplies the article and noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To snivel is to whine and grumble in a weepy, sniffling way.

clue.text: Edges to lightly cover with a stretchy fabric

indicators.note: edges are the outside, so only the first and last letters are kept

blocks.note: the outside letters only
the outside letters only
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions to trim the border with an elastic material.
explanation.definitionFit: Lycra is the brand name for spandex, an elastic synthetic fibre used in sportswear.

clue.text: Wasteful gourmand round bar with beer in short measure

indicators.note: the glutton goes round the bar, enclosing it
a short measure is a drink not filled up, so the beer loses its last letter

blocks.note: a pig is a greedy eater
a rod is a bar
ale is beer

explanation.surface: A greedy eater at the bar is short-changed on his beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub counter, but it is a rod of metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Prodigal means recklessly extravagant with money, as in the parable of the prodigal son.

clue.text: Seeing red in abattoir at Edgware

indicators.note: the letters are contained within the words that follow

blocks.note: from the end of the first word, the second, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Seeing blood at a slaughterhouse in Edgware, a north London suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seeing red' suggests blood in an abattoir; it is the idiom for anger.
explanation.definitionFit: To see red is an idiom for becoming suddenly furious, which describes an angry person.

clue.text: Brownish-orange peels from the tikka covering grated carrot

indicators.note: a peel is the outer skin, so only the outside letters are taken
grating reduces something to shreds, so its letters are scrambled
the outer letters wrap around the jumbled vegetable

blocks.note: the outside letters
the six letters to be shredded
the outside letters

explanation.surface: A curry topped with grated carrot glows reddish-orange.
explanation.definitionFit: Terracotta is unglazed fired clay, and its colour name is a brownish-orange shade.

clue.text: Line the writer grasps when climbing tree

indicators.note: what is grasped is held within, so one piece holds the other
in a down clue, climbing means reading upwards, from bottom to top

blocks.note: the writer means the setter, me
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A writer clings to a rope while climbing a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The elm is a large deciduous broadleaved tree, once common in English hedgerows.

clue.text: Old German wants no second extension to cell

indicators.note: wanting none of something means going without it, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: the Saxons were an ancient Germanic people
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: An elderly German prisoner wants no extra time in his cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cell' suggests a prison, but it is a nerve cell.
explanation.definitionFit: An axon is the long fibre of a nerve cell that carries impulses away from its body.

clue.text: Mature males on staff in film showing organisational incompetence

indicators.note: the earlier pieces are placed within the word for film

blocks.note: a film of moisture is a mist
to man is to staff
to age is to mature
taken as a synonym

explanation.surface: Older men on a film crew show they cannot organise anything.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' puts the mature males after staff, and all three go inside the film.
explanation.definitionFit: Mismanagement is handling an organisation badly, a failure to run things competently.
